title: Functions and Arrow Functions
summary: Wrap code so you can reuse it — and meet the shorter arrow style.
heading: Functions and Arrow Functions

blocks.text: A function is a chunk of code with a name, so you can run it whenever you need it instead of writing it again. You can hand it inputs (called parameters), and it can hand back a result (the return value).

blocks.caption: A function takes inputs and gives back a result.

blocks.label: Declaration

blocks.text: Arrow functions are just a shorter way to write the same thing. When the body is a single expression, you can drop the return and the curly braces.

cards.title: Normal

items: A function bundles up code you can reuse anytime.
Parameters are the inputs; return sends back the result.
Arrow functions are a shorter style: (a, b) => a + b.
If the body is a single expression, it returns on its own — no return needed.
